answer: Coordination Depth Pricing. Each identity pays a fee equal to the harmonic mean of its recent pairwise co-activity, so dense clusters subsidize sparsity. An attacker must sustain many distinct, low-overlap interaction histories to keep the mean near its nadir, which is expensive to fabricate. At the zenith, honest sparse agents pay little; the tundra of isolated sybils pays most. Cost is continuous history maintenance, not a one-time buy-in.
